The migration risk D28 was raised against is already closed by the canon half -- prose has somewhere to land, so WP-10 can no longer port a work package by dropping it. **VIEW ARM NOW LANDED (vc, 2026-08-15): `wp_prose_roundtrip.rs` renders the `WP/<NN>/info.md` view, carries authored sections verbatim, leaves the canon byte-identical, and renders the same bytes twice.** That was the whole remainder as this row last read it, so two of three arms are now green and guarded. **WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT AN UNBUILT ARM BUT AN UNGUARDED ONE, and it is the subtler failure: the search arm was verified ONCE, by hand, at `1ca760b`, and NOTHING TESTS IT.** `wp_prose_roundtrip.rs` says so in its own header -- "search half were verified independently" -- and `search_surface.rs` covers a WP **title**, which is not what this row requires: the discriminator is a phrase appearing only in a WP **body**, because a hit on the title could come from the parent thread's index entry. A property demonstrated once and guarded by nothing is a property that decays silently, which is the exact class this thread keeps catching. **CLOSED 2026-08-15, verified by vc: `a_phrase_only_in_a_work_package_body_is_found_and_names_the_work_package`.** All three arms now guarded. **cc mutation-proved the discriminator rather than asserting it, and the mutation is the evidence this row wanted: stop indexing WP bodies in ingest and `a_word_in_a_work_package_title_is_found` STAYS GREEN while only the new test fails.** The title test cannot discriminate a WP hit from its parent thread's, which is what this row claimed and what is now demonstrated

**Every flag the dispatch surface declares is READ by the renderer, or it is withdrawn from the surface. A declared-and-inert flag is a lie told by `--help`, and it is worse than an absent feature.** Raised by cc 2026-08-15 as a CLASS rather than as five fixes, and contracted here rather than left as a test cc invents, because the remedy for each instance is a scope decision and not a wiring job. **Five live instances, verified behaviourally rather than by grep**: `sync --to-disk` / `--to-store` (AC-03.9's own selector -- declared, helped, refused), `doctor --fix` (promises mutation, silently does nothing), `doctor --verbose` / `--quiet` (no effect), and `st new -s` / `--start` -- where `intent st new "a thread" -s` prints `created: ST0001` and the thread lands at `Triage`, **with no error and no effect**. **The failure is that an inert flag is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A WORKING ONE at the surface an operator actually reads**: help lists it, the parser accepts it, the exit code is 0. An operator who reads `--help` and runs `--to-disk` is told the thing they just read does not exist. **cc's census missed `st new -s` for the reason that makes this mechanical rather than diligence-shaped**: the long spelling is `start`, and that string is all over the renderer as a verb, so a grep found the spelling asked for while the claim had another one. Requires a check that walks the declared surface and fails naming any flag no renderer arm reads -- the same shape as AC-02.6's openness declarations, one artefact over. **MECHANISM RULED 2026-08-15 (vc) on ic's EXP-05, because this row demanded a withdrawal the surface could not perform.** ic measured that **the table can withdraw a COMMAND and cannot withdraw a FLAG**: `is_shipped()` gates an entry on `disposition` + `target.state`, while `spine.rs` builds every declared flag on every shipped entry unconditionally, and the flag schema has no field that could say otherwise. So this row and AC-06.9 both read "wire it, or do the thing that cannot be done" -- **a criterion whose satisfying action has no mechanism**, which is a contract defect of mine, not a build gap. **Adopted: a flag carries a `disposition` in the vocabulary entries already use -- `keep` ships and must be read; `retire` is recorded from v2 and never reaches clap; `pending` does NOT ship**, because an undecided flag on the surface IS the defect this row names. Every flag declares one, refused otherwise, same construction as the MCP fields -- so a flag cannot join the surface merely by being typed. **`pending` does NOT refuse the build**, ruled against the stricter option: a hard blocker on an undecided flag stops every node's build on a decision that is nobody's emergency, and a guard that must be bypassed is a guard nobody keeps. **But absence must not be silent** -- `doctor` reports the pending count, so the quiet-absence hazard ic correctly raised is answered somewhere that is not the build. **The arrival schedule is why this could not wait: 2 present violations and 44 declared-and-unread flags on commands with no renderer arm yet**, and those arrive ONE AT A TIME as each command is wired -- never a batch anyone confronts, each landing inside a commit about something else. **The RULING that resolves all five: wired or withdrawn, never advertised-and-inert.** Withdrawal is a legitimate answer and is the right one wherever the behaviour is unspecified -- see AC-06.9 for `doctor --fix`, which is the instance where wiring it would be the defect

**`doctor --fix` is specified before it is wired, or it is withdrawn from the surface.** cc declined to wire it and was right to. Every other doctor path REPORTS; a `--fix` that mutates canon is a different kind of verb wearing the same name. **Under D01 as reversed, "fix" against the store and "fix" against the extract are different operations with different blast radii** -- one edits durable truth, the other edits a projection that the next sync overwrites -- and the flag as declared says which of those it does. **Wiring it to something plausible is how a repair verb ends up owning a direction nobody chose**, which is the same failure D05's refusal posture exists to prevent and the same one AC-03.9 caught in `sync`. Requires, before any implementation: the finding classes it may touch, the classes it must refuse, and which side of the store/extract boundary it operates on. **RULED BY hv 2026-08-15: WITHDRAWN as a mutation** -- _"If doctor shows a suggested fix, do we need it? Happy to withdraw it for now as a mutation."_ **hv's question is the better half of the ruling and it generalises: a diagnostic that NAMES the exact remedy may be strictly better than one that performs it.** The operator sees what will happen, decides whether it is what they meant, and keeps the blast radius in their own hands -- which is D05's refusal posture arriving one level up, and the same reasoning as dc's "the control goes where the harm is" and cc's declining to wire it in the first place. **A repair verb is a claim that the tool understands the fault well enough to act on it unattended; a named remedy is a claim only that it understands it well enough to describe it, and the second claim is the one `doctor` can actually make.** So the criterion is met by the WITHDRAWAL arm: `--fix` comes off the declared surface, and `doctor`'s findings each carry a remedy string an operator can read and run themselves. **It is "for now", not "never"** -- re-adding it is cheap once someone can state the finding classes it may touch, the classes it must refuse, and which side of the store/extract boundary it operates on. **This row goes green when the flag is GONE from the dispatch table and the renderer, not when the ruling is recorded** -- the ruling is hv's and is done; the removal is ic's (the declared row) and cc's (the renderer arm) -- **THE WITHDRAWAL MECHANISM IS `disposition: retire` (AC-06.8), and `--fix` is its first user.** `retire` means exactly this: recorded from v2, never reaches clap. v2's `bin/intent_doctor` does implement `-f|--fix`, so it is a real v2 behaviour we are deliberately not carrying -- **which is precisely what `retire` is for, as distinct from `pending`.** Measured at the same time and ruled with it: **`--verbose` and `--quiet` are `pending`, NOT `retire`** -- v2's doctor genuinely implements them (a `verbose()` function and colour suppression under quiet), so they are behaviours to be wired rather than promises to be dropped

criteria.text: **Every published schema face carries `INTENT_VER` and `SCHEMA_<TYPE>_VER`, injected from code and discoverable without parsing the artefact** (D41, hv 2026-08-15). Three face types -- `SCHEMA_JSON_VER`, `SCHEMA_DDL_VER`, `SCHEMA_SDL_VER` -- across five files, matching AC-06.5's count; the three JSON Schemas share one version because they are one contract in three documents, and splitting per file would let `thread` and `issue` drift apart with nothing saying they had. **The two parts answer different questions and move at different rates**: `INTENT_VER` says which tool produced the artefact, `SCHEMA_<TYPE>_VER` says whether the contract a consumer compiles against has changed. A patch release moves the first and must not move the second. Requires: **(a)** the versions are constants in code and the generator injects them into each face in that face's own idiom -- **hand-writing a version into a generated artefact recreates the exact defect this closes**, which is the "generated artefact with a hand-kept companion" pattern this thread met three times in one day; **(b)** a surface reports both parts for every face, so a consumer deciding whether to upgrade can ASK rather than diff; and **(c)** AC-06.5's byte-identity property holds WITH the versions present, so the injected values are compared rather than exempted. **Measured before ruling (vc, 2026-08-15): zero occurrences of "version" in any of the five faces**, while the internal never-committed store had carried `SCHEMA_VERSION` and a hard refusal since that morning -- the internal artefact versioned and the external contract not, which is backwards, because the store rebuilds from the extract and a consumer's code rebuilds from nothing we hold. **Deliberately NOT extended to help text**: changing a help string breaks nobody's code. **The line is whether a consumer COMPILES against it**, which is also why the instrument is a version and not a text baseline -- a baseline tells us something changed, a version tells the consumer

**Every remedy the binary suggests names something the binary can actually do.** **WIDENED 2026-08-15 (vc) on ic's measurement, deliberately as ONE row rather than two**: the property is that a remedy is ACTIONABLE, and it fails identically whether the remedy names a verb that does not exist or a verb-SPACE that does not exist. **Measured: 17 commands are unimplemented and NINE are leaves with zero verbs** -- `info`, `init`, `bootstrap`, `learn`, `fileindex`, `version`, `export`, `ingest`, `mcp` -- and each sends the user to `run intent <cmd> --help for the verbs that are`, a `--help` listing no verbs at all. **One property over one corpus, the emitted remedies**, which is the test: I split the schema faces off AT-00.8 the same afternoon on a corpus argument and had to reverse it within the hour when the corpus turned out to be the same one. (vc 2026-08-15, ruled to the contract on dc's question rather than into `int macos publish`, which is where dc proposed it and correctly declined to build it.) **Live instance**: `brew install` puts v3 at PATH position 1 while a v2 install sits at 17 and 19, so a v2 user meets v3's unmigrated-project refusal without having asked for anything -- and **that refusal's remedy names `intent upgrade`, which the v3 binary does not have** (`migration.md:3` says the migrator IS that verb, so it is WP-10 unbuilt, not a wrong string). **The ruling is about WHERE the control goes, and it is what un-couples WP-11 from WP-10.** dc could have made `publish` refuse to ship a binary whose remedies name unreachable verbs, and declined because gating publish on another work package's progress is a sequencing ruling wearing a mechanism's clothes. **That objection is right, and it dissolves once the check moves**: the harm is not "we published", it is "a binary tells a user to run a verb it does not have" -- **a property of the artefact, true the moment the string is written and equally true of a binary nobody ever publishes.** A publish-time gate catches it at the last possible moment, on the node least able to fix it, and only if a release happens; a build-time invariant fires when the string lands, on whoever wrote it, and asserts something true of v3 independent of when `upgrade` arrives. Requires a check that walks every operator-facing remedy string and fails naming any that references a verb the surface does not carry -- **the same shape as AC-06.8's declared-versus-read walk, one artefact over.** Its acceptance test is **held RED with an explicit note** until WP-10 lands `upgrade` (the AT-06.4 / AT-06.7 practice): **a red row with a note is the honest state and names its dependency, where a missing check reads as covered**

The critic headless runner reads embedded rules and preserves the ST0039 strict-proxy contract **ELABORATED 2026-08-18 (vc), ruling dc's fleet-default question, because a ruling that lives only in a peer's inbox is not a contract.** **THE MEASURED STARTING POINT, WHICH NOTHING HAD: all 13 shell and rust rules carry NO proxy AND NO declaration, and `critic_runner.sh:18` SKIPS A PROXY-LESS RULE SILENTLY -- so `critic shell` and `critic rust` return rc=0 because nothing was ever asked. 13 of 13.** (dc 2026-08-18.) A green from a runner that asked no question is the swallow this estate forbids, and it is present TODAY, before any rule is armed. **(a) UNCONDITIONAL, AND NOT PART OF ANY TRADE-OFF: a rule the runner could not check is REPORTED -- named, with WHICH of three reasons applies (no proxy / no declaration / tool absent).** Reporting is not refusing; it costs no consumer anything and is owed however the rest is ruled. **(b) REFUSAL IS SCOPED TO A RULE THE PROJECT ARMED, and arming is the OPT-IN.** A project with no `.intent_critic.yml` has armed nothing, so nothing refuses and upgrade day is uneventful for it. **hv's ruling -- a tool-armed rule REFUSES when its tool is absent -- applies unweakened to the case it names: a project that armed a rule and then lost the tool** (a CI image change, a machine without shellcheck) is refused, not silently passed. **(c) THE DILEMMA DISSOLVES BECAUSE ITS TWO HORNS SHARED A FALSE PREMISE.** dc posed refuse-by-default (honest, and a fleet-wide breakage on upgrade day) against optional-by-default (safe, and _the invisible failure with a friendlier name_). **The invisibility was never a property of OPTIONAL; it was a property of the SILENT SKIP.** Fix the silence and an un-opted-in project is told, on every run, which rules are unenforced and what would enforce them -- **unenforced-and-stated is not invisible.** Nothing forced optional and silent together except the runner. **AND THE NAMED-TOOL BOUNDARY GAINS ITS WORKED EXAMPLE, WHICH NEEDS NO ADVERSARY** (dc, measured against clippy 0.1.97): `IN-RS-CODE-001`'s remedy is the **ABSENCE** of `--all-targets` -- default `cargo clippy` flags a production `.unwrap()` and not a colocated `#[cfg(test)]` one. **A rule file naming that flag would be a rule file contributing shell in order to make a lint see LESS.** The rule names WHICH tool; the runner owns HOW. **`critic_proxy_is_simple` remains an injection boundary and is not relaxed.** **A DECLARE-NONE MUST SAY WHY IT IS ONE:** `IN-SH-CODE-004` is declare-none because **shellcheck refuses zsh outright (`SC1071`) -- no tool exists** -- not because the runner is narrow, and those are different sentences to whoever reads the output next.

**CORRECTION 2026-08-20 (vc, against my own elaboration above, driven at zero hops on build `sha256 326990c5597284e7`). THE CLAUSE _a project with no `.intent_critic.yml` has armed nothing_ IS FALSE, AND IT WAS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT FOR THE WHOLE RULING.** That file carries `severity_min`, a `disabled:` list and `post_tool_use_advisory`, and **no arming key of any kind**. Arming is declared by the RULE -- `IN-SH-CODE-001(shellcheck)` -- never by the project. Driven: a scratch project with no yml at all, shellcheck hidden from PATH, one shell file -> **v2 exits 3**, and adding the yml changes nothing. **So the opt-in that 'upgrade day is uneventful for it' rests on does not exist.** The true statement is narrower and still sound: refusal is scoped to a rule that is ARMED and whose LANGUAGE the project declared, and **the opt-out is the `disabled:` list, not the file's absence.** The (c) dissolution is untouched -- unenforced-and-stated is still not invisible, and that never depended on the yml.

**THE SAME DRIVE FOUND (b) UNIMPLEMENTED IN v3, AND IT IS THE SHAPE OF INV-04 ONE FILE OVER.** Tool absent, `IN-SH-CODE-001` and `IN-SH-CODE-002` armed: **both binaries REPORT the absence correctly and name both rules -- case (a) is at parity -- and then v2 exits 3 while v3 exits 0.** The cause is two meanings of one word, stated five lines apart in v3's own file: `critic.rs:37` gives the header table _3 = refused -- a rule was armed and could not be enforced here_, which is this criterion's meaning, while `critic.rs:225` declares `refused` as _rules whose PROXY the contract refused_, which is ST0039's. `render.rs:3042` keys `Failure::Refused` on the latter, so exit 3 fires for a refused proxy and **never** for `not-run:tool-absent`. v2 sets `CRITIC_REFUSED=1` inside the `c_absent` block at `intent_critic:319`, a different condition entirely. **A machine missing shellcheck -- a CI image, a new laptop -- silently passes what hv ruled must block, and it passes every test that exists.**

The typed tool tier is generated from the dispatch table with schemars-derived parameter schemas. **Each entry DECLARES two fields the generator needs and the table does not carry today -- whether it is exposed on the MCP surface, and whether it READS or MUTATES -- and a row declaring neither is REFUSED.** (ic, EXP-03, raised 2026-08-15 before WP-09 opened, by reading this AC against the artefact it names.) Measured across all 103 rows: neither fact is present or derivable. `observed.side_effects` sits on 10 of 103, so **its absence means "not recorded", not "no side effects"** -- absence-as-meaning in the one place it decides whether an agent may close a steel thread. Without the fields a generator has exactly two options and both are defects: expose everything, so `intent mcp` becomes a tool that starts an MCP server from inside one; or carry a skip list, which is **a hand-maintained command list living one command away from AC-09.4, which forbids hand-maintained command lists** -- correct when typed and silently wrong at the next command added, because the act that invalidates it is not the act that updates it. **DECLARED per row, never derived from the verb**, and the proof that derivation fails is in the surface itself: `st sync` and `sync` are different commands sharing a spelling, and **`ac gate` reads while `wp done` consults the same gate and writes**. The refusal is what makes it hold -- with it there is no default to drift; **for a HUMAN resolving an uncertain row the safe directions are opposite** (`exposed` defaults toward no, `mutates` defaults toward yes), since a command wrongly omitted is an inconvenience and one wrongly included lets an agent run `daemon`, and a mutation mislabelled as a read lets an agent close a thread believing it is querying. **EXTENDED 2026-08-17 (vc, on ic's finding, under hv's standing grant): the generated tool DESCRIPTION -- not only the parameter schema -- carries `read_or_mutate` and, for a mutation, `recoverability`, in the D45 projection order the CLI guide already uses.** As written this AC obliged the generator to describe a tool's ARGUMENTS and obliged it to say nothing about what calling it does to the estate. **The consequence is already declared in the table and is not hypothetical: `at green`, `at red`, `at na` and `ext new` are all `exposed_on_mcp: true` AND `recoverability: one-way`** -- one-way because issue 0033 destroys the row's authored note, 1,447 characters measured on AT-03.12 and 14,253 at risk across 34 rows. **So the identical destructive operation would warn a CLI agent at the point of call and say nothing at all to an MCP agent**, which is the surface with less context. **D45 does not license the omission and reading it that way inverts it**: hv ruled the CLI precise and MCP imprecise, and `imprecise` is a claim about capability granularity, not about disclosure -- an agent with less context needs the safety fact more, not less. **This invents no policy and adds no field**: `recoverability`, its vocabulary, its refusal and its renderer all exist and are proven on the CLI surface, and this is one more projection of the same declaration, which is the whole argument for why `recoverability` is intrinsic to a row rather than an exposure flag. **Ruled BEFORE the tier is built deliberately** -- today it costs a sentence in an AC, and after WP-09 it is a change to what agents have already been told. **Sharpened by `design.md:310-320`, which is the same cut**: `schemars` lifts `///` into the JSON Schemas and a `///` on a derived type is _"an unreviewed publication channel -- the author is writing a comment and the consumer is reading a contract"_. **The generated description will carry prose either way; the only question this settles is whether that prose is the safety fact or whatever doc comment happens to sit on the type.**

A pre-2.19.0 project is refused with the two-hop instruction named. **CLOSED SAME DAY: found unsatisfied 2026-08-17 (vc), fixed by cc at `f2b7b97a`, re-measured satisfied by vc against the same estate -- `intent upgrade` on pinned Utilz now exits 1 naming `2.18.0`, the `v2.19.0` floor and `install intent@2`, writes nothing (101/101 verified, stamp untouched), while the 2.19.0 canary still converts.** The fix is one arm before `legacy::scan` -- refuse iff `Pending { below_floor: true }`, remedy delegated to `Pending::remedy()` rather than copied -- and a distinct `BelowMigrationFloor` variant rather than reusing `Unmigrated`, because both carry the same data and **the operator's situation differs**: _this project has not been migrated_ is news to someone who asked a question and a restatement of their own intent to someone who just ran the migrator. The record of the original finding follows, because how it was found is the reusable part. **MEASURED UNSATISFIED 2026-08-17 (vc), against the only real pre-2.19.0 estate in the fleet corpus: Utilz declares `2.18.0` and `Facade::upgrade` MIGRATED it** -- 61 files, 9 threads, 19 carried findings, no refusal, and `config.json` left reading `3.0.0-dev`. **The mechanism is a floor enforced on the door that READS and not on the door that WRITES**: `Facade::open` calls `Self::readable()`, which returns `FacadeError::Unmigrated(pending)` whose `remedy()` is delegated precisely so the sub-floor case gets the two-hop (`facade.rs:406` says so); `Facade::upgrade` never calls `readable()` and goes straight to `legacy::scan`. **Why it is worse than a missing guard: the two-hop exists because 2.19.0 is where the AT row grammar landed**, so a 2.18.0 estate migrated straight to v3 skips that migration and its AT rows arrive in a grammar v3 was never told about, silently, because nothing on this path is looking. AT-10.1 (`migrate_floor.rs`) is `to-write`, so this is an unbuilt criterion with a measurement attached rather than a regression. **It could only have been found by a real sub-floor estate** -- the canary and Lamplight and Baize all declare 2.19.0, and a constructed fixture would have been built by someone who already knew the floor was the question

A **2.19.0 project that has not yet been migrated** is detected and named as such by every command that reads the model -- never answered from an empty model as though the estate were empty. Measured at WP-06 on this repository (195 `info.md`, zero `thread.json`): `intent st list` returned **exit 0 with zero bytes on both streams** where v2 returns a 276-byte table, and `doctor` reported "2 findings across 0 threads" with both findings being view-skew derived from rendering an empty model against real files -- a confident false RED at the exact moment of a user's first contact with v3. AC-10.1 covers pre-2.19.0 and the migration itself is AC-00.8/AC-10.3; the state BETWEEN -- v3 installed, project at 2.19.0, canon not yet written -- was unspecified, and it is the state every project on earth is in the first time v3 runs. **Swept across the read surface at `2e490e5` (vc), and one root produces three symptoms, of which the second is worse than the one this AC was written from**: (a) **silent-empty** -- `st list` and `search` exit 0 with zero bytes on both streams; (b) **a confident false negative BY NAME** -- `wp list ST0056`, `ac status ST0056`, `at list ST0056` and `st show ST0056` each exit 1 with `error: no steel thread ST0056 in this project` while `intent/st/ST0056/info.md` sits on disk being edited; (c) **a false RED** -- `doctor`. (b) is the dangerous one: silence is ambiguous and invites a second look, whereas a specific denial is actionable, and the obvious action on "no steel thread ST0056" is to create it -- on top of the real one. In an agentic context that is a destructive read. The remaining read commands (`issues`, `todo`, `info`, `config`, `version`) refuse honestly as unwired and name the owing WP, which is the correct shape and the standard the three symptoms above should be held to

**Egest symmetry**: deleting the file estate and egesting from the DB reproduces it, and the only difference is the out-of-model set enumerated at `data-model.md`, **named in the output rather than silently absent**. The second half of ic's proposal, accepted 2026-08-15. **Its original justification is VOID under D36 and is replaced rather than reworded**: it read that "`rm intent.db` is safe only if files remain to ingest back from, and vice versa", which prices this AC in an operation that does not exist. **The property it actually tests is unchanged and is stronger stated directly: the two directions must be inverses, so that the extract is a faithful carrier of the DB and not merely a plausible one.** That is D34's precondition -- the extract is the interchange, so a field that egests wrong is data loss at the clone boundary -- and it needs no deletion scenario to matter. What made the old framing worth keeping is the half it exposed, which survives intact: the fleet acceptance fixture tests ingest forward only, and explicitly on semantic completeness rather than byte round-trip. Accepted on the failure shape rather than the feature: this is exactly the class that failed on ic's `burn-baseline.tsv`, where the header asserted the artefact reproduced the register, everyone believed it, nothing checked, and it drifted three rows in silence -- with the difference that an untested egest guarantee only fails on the day someone has already lost the files. **A project can still COMMIT with v3 installed -- MIGRATED OR NOT -- asserted end-to-end through the shipped hook rather than by inspecting hook files.** (vc 2026-08-16, on dc's issue 0038, measured end to end.) **This is a new criterion rather than a widening of AC-10.4, and the distinction is the finding.** AC-10.4 asserts `.claude/settings.json` + `.claude/scripts/**` are byte-identical pre/post -- and dc's measurement is that **byte-identical hooks plus a changed exit code is a broken gate that byte-identity reports GREEN.** A file-identity criterion cannot see a semantic break, so widening its path list to include `.git/hooks` would add coverage in the axis that already works and none in the axis that failed. **`.git/hooks` is covered by no AC in this thread and never was, which is why nothing caught this.** The measured failure: a migrated project with `languages: ["shell"]` and one staged file gets `error: \`critic\` is a known command that is not implemented yet`followed by`commit blocked by findings at severity >= warning`, **and the remedy cannot be followed because there is no finding.** The only escape is `--no-verify`. **The exit-code contract is the mechanism and v2 honours it: the gate reserves 1 for "your code has findings" and 2+ for "the critic tooling itself is unavailable", and `intent critic nosuchlang`exits 2 under v2.** v3 collapsed unavailable into the code meaning your-code-is-bad, so the gate's fail-open branch exists, is correct, and is never reached. **Wider than`critic`**: `agents`and`llm`(not implemented),`organize`and`treeindex`(unrecognised subcommand) and a missing`<LANG>`(usage error) all exit 1 -- three different kinds of event sharing one code, of which only the last is arguably the caller's fault. **Severity is set by 0036 rather than by this bug alone:`brew install`SHADOWS a v2 install, so first contact is in a project the user was not thinking about, and the gate refuses everything in it.** And it trains the bypass -- the first`--no-verify`is correct and unavoidable, and the habit outlives the cause. **Ordering consequence worth stating because it is a scheduling decision and not a coding one: WP-10 landing before WP-07 puts every migrated project in this state.** **WIDENED 2026-08-17 (vc, on issue 0045) from "a migrated project" to "migrated or not", and the widening is the point rather than a tidy-up.** The original wording was written against dc's 0038, whose fixture is migrated because that is what 0038 was about -- so the criterion, the test cc built from it, and every instrument pointed at it all inherited that scope, and **the UNMIGRATED project, which is the state every project in the estate is in until WP-10 runs on it, was covered by nothing.** Measured 2026-08-17:`Facade::open`gates on migration before anything else, the refusal maps to`EXIT_ERROR`, and the pre-commit gate reads 1 as *blocked by findings* -- so a commit in an unmigrated project is refused with `review the findings above, fix them, and re-commit`over a project that has none. **It does not reproduce today, and only because`critic`is unbuilt and exits 2 into the fail-open branch**, which is a reprieve nobody chose and that ends the moment WP-07 lands. **Two arms, both driven end to end through the shipped`pre-commit.sh` against a command that reaches the facade: migrated commits, and unmigrated commits.** Widened rather than split into a new AC because -- unlike the AC-10.4 case argued above, where the axis genuinely differed -- this is the same axis, the same instrument and the same consumer, with only the project state changed; a second criterion here would be two rows asking one question.

**A migrated project's whiteboard guards still REFUSE what they refused before the swap** -- asserted by driving the shipped hook and watching it BLOCK, never by checking that the guard files are present. (vc 2026-08-16, issue 0042, measured.) **This is the gap in my own AC-10.9 and the distinction is the same one that made 10.9 a new criterion rather than a widening of 10.4.** AC-10.9 asks whether a migrated project can commit; **a commit that succeeds with both guards silently not running satisfies it completely.** Necessary, not sufficient. The measured cause: `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh:104` resolves the guard directory with `intent info 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *INTENT_HOME: *//p'`, **v3 did not implement `info`, the value came back EMPTY, and both guards took the hook's fail-open branch.** **CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (cc, measured; vc verified): THIS NO LONGER REPRODUCES.** `intent info` now resolves, and the hook's own extraction run against the v3 binary returns the real path rather than nothing. **The resolver's live failure mode is a different one and it is about INSTALL LOCATION, not about `info` being unimplemented**: the value is `<not set>` when the binary sits outside its install, which cc hit in a worktree. **The criterion itself is UNAFFECTED and is the reason it was written as a behaviour rather than as a bug**: it demands the guards be shown to REFUSE by driving the shipped hook, which no longer has a known way to fail and therefore has no evidence either. **Two further corrections to this row's own text, and the second is my own rule biting me**: the cited `pre-commit.sh:104` has drifted -- line 104 is now a comment -- so the citation is to a line number rather than to a thing; and a criterion whose measured cause is fixed while the criterion stands is exactly the state that needs saying out loud, because the alternative is a row that reads as an open defect when what is open is the absence of proof. **It is independent of the exit code, which is why `d2b8e76d` could not have touched it -- the hook reads stdout and `2>/dev/null` discards the error either way.** **And it is the worse shape of the pair: 0038 failed CLOSED, so it was loud, blocking, and fixed inside a day; this fails OPEN, so the commit succeeds and the only symptom is a line on stderr during a green commit.** The controls at stake are not decorative -- the clock guard refused a commit carrying a fabricated timestamp after six prose resolutions of the same rule had failed to stop the previous six, and the header guard is newer still and has the least field time of any control in the estate. **Intent's own dogfood migration hits this** (this repo has `intent/whiteboard/`) **and so does Lamplight, second in the corpus.** The fix is forced rather than chosen: 0016 forbids rewiring the hook and a silent exit 0 is a silent failure, so implementing `info` is what remains -- **but the durable half is that a hook must not resolve a path by parsing a display command's output**, since nothing in `info` declares itself machine-read and nothing in the hook declares it needs `info`

**An INTERRUPTED migration and an uninterrupted one reach the same end state, and the interruption is DEMONSTRATED rather than simulated.** (vc 2026-08-18, minted on the moratorium lift; the instruments predated the criterion.) A partial run killed mid-flight and then re-run must produce the estate an uninterrupted run produces -- **and the evidence must show the kill was real**, since a hand-rolled partial write proves only that the harness can truncate a file. The discriminating artefact is the temp-and-rename residue a real process death leaves and a simulated one never does. **Both readings must be taken against a BINARY PINNED BY CONTENT HASH, never by its self-reported provenance marker** (ic 2026-08-18, on a live casualty): a marker can stay byte-identical across two behaviourally different builds, so a paired reading keyed on the marker certifies pairs that are not pairs. **AND THIS IS NOT A `dirty-` WORKAROUND (dc 2026-08-18): NO PROVENANCE MARKER OF ANY DESIGN CAN DISTINGUISH TWO BUILDS OF ONE SOURCE**, so a future clean marker fails identically. The pin is by content hash because the property required is byte identity of the ARTEFACT, which no self-report can carry.

A tagged version yields installable artefacts and a working tap formula for both binaries, such that `brew install` on a machine that has never seen this repo produces a runnable `intent` and `intentd`. **REWRITTEN 2026-08-15 (vc) on dc's measurement, and the rewrite is the finding: this row named cargo-dist as its mechanism and demanded "release CI run" as its evidence, and both were wrong in a way that made the row unsatisfiable by the approach the estate has already validated.** cargo-dist 0.32.0 **does not notarise at all** (`strings`: `notarytool`, `notariz`, `stapler`, `altool`, `xcrun` -- zero hits each); it signs only, via a base64 p12 imported from a CI secret into a temp keychain. D38 requires both binaries signed **and** notarised unconditionally, so the named mechanism covers at most half of the criterion beside it, and covers that half by exporting the signing identity out of the login Keychain into a repository secret -- strictly worse than `int macos sign|notarize|verify`, which is proven end to end and keeps the identity in the Keychain. **The general rule this row now carries: AN AC NAMES THE OUTCOME, AND THE MECHANISM BELONGS IN THE WORK PACKAGE.** A criterion that names a tool can be invalidated by a measurement of that tool while the thing the project actually wanted is still perfectly achievable -- which is exactly what happened here, and it cost a rewrite rather than a rethink only because dc measured before wiring. **SCOPED BY hv RULING 2026-08-15 (D39, D40): macOS arm64 ONLY, tap `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent`, artefacts on the source repo's own releases, cargo-dist DEFERRED.** So the mechanism is the local `int macos sign|notarize|stage|formula` path and the row no longer has a tool question in it. **The evidence line is now STRONGER than the one it replaced, not weaker**: a CI run proves a pipeline executed, whereas a `brew install` actually run once proves the artefact, the checksum, the formula and the tap all agree -- which is the only claim this row was ever making. **BLOCKER CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (vc, on dc's report, both claims re-measured rather than relayed): ONE of the two named blockers was cleared two days ago and this row went on asserting it.** `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` **exists** -- `gh repo view --json createdAt,isEmpty` returns `2026-08-15T15:19:58Z`, `isEmpty: false`, created the afternoon after this row was written. **dc's distinction is kept because the row needs it: `isEmpty: false` means "has a commit", NOT "has a formula"** -- the tap holds one README explaining why it is deliberately empty, which is the state this row's own argument below calls for. So the tap is not a blocker and never was after 2026-08-15; the absent FORMULA is a deliberate choice. **What IS still live is the version: `Cargo.toml:6` declares `3.0.0-dev` and the release binary reports it, and the publish step refuses to emit a formula for a dev build.** That is held deliberately until WP-12, because wiring `Cargo.toml` into `int build release`'s sidecar sync now would make a **v2** release stamp its version into it. **AND THE ROW REFUTED ITSELF BEFORE ANYONE NOTICED, WHICH IS THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX**: the stale clause said the tap "does not exist yet" while a later sentence in the SAME row says "the tap is deliberately LIVE AND EMPTY" and reasons from it. Two clauses of one criterion contradicting each other, added at different times, with nothing comparing them -- **so the row was not merely stale, it was internally inconsistent, and a reader could quote either half.** **The general rule, and it is the mirror of AC-00.9's**: a criterion that carries its own EVIDENCE decays exactly like a measurement that names a revision, and this one decayed in our favour -- someone could have spent an afternoon creating a repository that already existed. A stale blocker reads as current work whichever direction it decayed. **REQUIRED REFUSAL, from dc 2026-08-15: the PUBLISH step refuses to emit a formula for a dev build.** dc's framing is the rule and it generalises past this row -- **the control goes where the HARM is, which is publication, not printing.** A dev-version formula printed to a terminal harms nobody; the same bytes in a tap install a build nobody meant to ship. **The tap is deliberately LIVE AND EMPTY on the same reasoning, and it is the better half of the argument**: dc had a generated, verified formula in hand and did not push it, because it would have pointed at a release tag that does not exist -- so `brew tap` SUCCEEDS and `brew install` fails with a download error, and **a user reads "the tap is broken" when the truth is "the release is not out yet". A wrong artefact is not a neutral placeholder; it makes a confident false statement, where an empty tap says the true thing**

criteria.text: The binary is fully functional with no INTENT_HOME in the environment **and the variable is not read at all, which is stronger than an override and is deliberate** **PARENTHETICAL CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (vc), on dc's measurement, on a row that is already GREEN -- which is where a stale claim survives, because nothing re-examines a closed criterion (issue 0032, this contract's own weighing).** The row read _"demoted to dev override"_, and **there is no override: `$INTENT_HOME` is never read from the environment.** Measured by dc on one binary three ways -- set in the environment: `<not set>`; absent: `<not set>`; from inside an install: the real path -- and confirmed by vc at source, where **zero `var("INTENT_HOME")` or `var_os("INTENT_HOME")` calls exist in any crate.** `intent info` self-locates by walking up from its resolved executable path. **THE MAIN CLAUSE IS TRUE AND THE GREEN STANDS**; AT-11.3 proves the binary is fully functional without the variable. It is the parenthetical that described a mechanism which does not exist -- **and the danger of leaving it is that a reader implementing to the contract would build the override back, which is precisely what happened once already: the first version of `install.rs` built one, and ic's `no_intent_home.rs` refused it.** **THE REASON IT MUST NEVER EXIST, hoisted here out of `install.rs:20` where it has been living as a code comment (cc):** the assets are VERSIONED, and `lib/templates/.claude/scripts/` in a v2 install and a v3 install are **different files with the same names**. A machine mid-rollout has both trees and a `$INTENT_HOME` left over from v2, so an override would make the v3 binary exec **v2's hook scripts**, silently, from a variable the operator set years earlier for a different tool. **The environment cannot know which version is running; the executable's own location always does.** **THAT IS WHY THIS IS A CONTRACT EDIT AND NOT A COMMENT: a ratified reason living in a transcription is found only by whoever next touches that transcription (cc's own rule, third instance today), and the contract is what a builder reads first.** **AND THE FIXTURE THAT FOUND IT PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON FIRST:** dc's first attempt set the variable and PASSED, because `cargo test` puts the binary under `target/` inside the repository, so walking up found a tree with `lib/templates/` in it. **The variable was doing nothing and the LAYOUT was doing all of it.** It surfaced only under a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, which moved the build out of the tree -- the subject moving out from under the instrument, caught by moving it deliberately.

**The published checksum matches the bytes the user downloads.** Signing and checksumming are ORDERED and the order is silent when wrong: `codesign --force` **rewrites the binary in place**, whereas `notarytool submit` uploads a zip of a copy and we cannot staple a bare Mach-O, so notarisation leaves the file byte-identical. Therefore **sign BEFORE you checksum; notarise whenever.** Get it backwards and the formula ships a sha256 computed over pre-signature bytes -- which never fails for us and fails for **every single `brew install`**, at the point in the pipeline where we have the least visibility. Raised by dc 2026-08-15 from the Conflab port, where two sha256 lines are hand-maintained in the formula and a `release sync` command exists partly to heal this class of drift. **Hand-maintained checksums beside a generated artefact is the same shape as the hand-kept `SCHEMA_VERSION` beside the DDL in AC-02.7**, and it wants the same answer: the release path computes the checksum from the artefact it just signed, or a check refuses the publish. **MECHANISM BUILT 2026-08-15 (dc) as `int macos stage`, ahead of this row and independently of it**: it names artefacts per target triple from `rustc -vV` rather than `uname` (the artefact name is a claim about what the compiler targeted, and only the compiler can answer that), proves each **staged copy**, refuses outright unless every artefact is both signed and notarised, and only then checksums. **RESTRUCTURED at `3ab8844e` and this row is corrected to match (dc reported the drift; vc ruled): `stage` now COPIES ONLY and `checksum` proves-then-hashes, with `prepare` running stage/sign/notarize/checksum as one pass.** The staged copies are what get SIGNED, in a directory only `int macos` writes, so the de-notarisation race shrinks from the whole multi-minute sequence spanning a round trip to Apple down to one `ditto`. **And the refusal deliberately no longer deletes the staging directory** -- it removes only `SHA256SUMS.txt` and leaves both binaries in place. That was harmless when staging copied the build output; it is actively wrong now the staged files carry a signature and a notarisation, because discarding them spends another Apple round trip rebuilding something already correct. **The stale CLAIM cannot survive while the WORK does, which is the right split**: `formula` treats that file's existence as its proof, so removing it is sufficient to make the refusal binding. Canaried in both directions, which is the part that makes it evidence: a control that has only ever refused proves as little as one that has only ever passed. **The row stays unsatisfied because nothing is published yet** -- the mechanism existing is not the criterion; the published hash matching the published bytes is. **Two things to carry into the release path when the matrix is ruled:** the staged copies should be SIGNED rather than copied-after-signing, so the signed artefact lives where only the release pipeline writes (dc recorded the inversion and deliberately did not refactor proven code ahead of the ruling); and `verify_notarised` must stay ONE implementation serving both `verify` and `stage`, because a release-time check that is a second copy of the development-time one is a check that drifts. **STRENGTHENED 2026-08-17 (dc reported; vc ruled, and dc was right that the row always meant this): CONSISTENCY IS NOT CORRESPONDENCE.** Every check in this pipeline -- the round trip, the sums file, the classification refusal, the tag-exists check -- asks whether the bytes agree with EACH OTHER, and **a set of bytes built from a peer's uncommitted work is perfectly self-consistent.** Nothing asked whether these are the bytes the TAG names, so `publish` could establish that a tag exists and then publish artefacts with no evidence they came from it. **Two reachable routes, neither hypothetical**: `stage` COPIES out of `native/rust/target/release` rather than building, and that directory is shared mutable state in a clone four nodes write to (dc has twice measured a rebuild adopting a peer's in-flight edit); and the support tarball is archived with `tar -C "$ROOT"` from the WORKING TREE, so uncommitted shell ships verbatim -- and `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh` was dirty for most of 2026-08-17. **Fixed by recording the commit at `stage` and refusing at `publish`, compared against the TAG's commit rather than HEAD** (publishing may legitimately happen after the branch moves on; a HEAD comparison looks correct and would refuse every late publish, and there is a mutant for exactly that). **So the evidence line grows a second half rather than being replaced**: the checksum half proves the artefact is intact, and the commit half proves it is the RIGHT artefact, and neither implies the other

**An artefact asserts its own provenance, and the assertion is READ FROM THE ARTEFACT, never from a record written beside it.** (vc 2026-08-17, on dc's finding; dc asked whether to strengthen AC-11.4 and the ruling is that this is a different criterion.) **A manifest states what was MEANT to be built; only the artefact can answer what was.** Three states are currently indistinguishable, all measured live and unplanted rather than constructed. **(a) The signed binary cannot name its commit**: `int macos stage` records `commit: <HEAD>` and `traceable: yes` -- where traceable means the working tree is clean -- and never asks when the binaries were BUILT, because `stage` copies them rather than building them. Measured with HEAD at `2026-08-17T15:11:14Z`: `intent` built three hours earlier, `intentd` **forty-two hours** earlier, forty-two hours apart from each other. Commit the tree and the whole chain goes green over bytes from two different earlier trees. **(b) The vendored tree cannot name its source**: `int vendor` compares the vendored files against a manifest that ships beside them and is rewritten by the same act that changes them, so a re-vendor and a local patch produce the identical `27 of 27`; and `devbin_version: 0.1.0` cannot separate them either, because **the field that exists to carry provenance is constant across exactly the thing it must distinguish.** **(c) An UNCOMMITTED REGENERATION is invisible to both** (dc, correcting their own report and vc's explanation of it): a tree that agrees with itself because someone re-derived the record locally is indistinguishable from a tree that agrees because it is correct. Measured at HEAD `702b58f8`: `bin/devbin` is `41017e54` while the manifest committed beside it records `8016f112`, so **a fresh clone reports DIVERGED right now** -- and every local check ran green throughout, over a regenerated manifest that was never committed. Verified by vc that `upstream/main` at `5765c5da` is self-consistent, so nothing broken is published; **that containment is an artefact of hv's CI-budget freeze and is recorded as luck rather than as a control**, because filing it as a save would teach the opposite of what happened. **Requires two things, and the second is what closes (c)**: the artefact carries its own source commit, embedded at build time and read back FROM the binary -- dc's own `staged_version` already argues this one function over, read the version from the BINARY and never from a manifest; and every provenance check compares against what the COMMIT holds rather than the worktree, for the same reason the whiteboard clock guard's check C blocks only on what the commit adds. **This is deliberately NOT folded into AC-11.4.** That row's criterion is _the published hash matching the published bytes_, which stale binaries satisfy perfectly -- the hash is honest and the commit attribution is not. Folding a provenance control under a checksum row would make a green start meaning something the row's text does not say, **which is the third axis (a remedy whose subject is not the report's) arriving inside a remedy.** dc declined to do it unprompted and asked first **MARKER CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (vc): this row carried the doc-check marker, and that made it UNCLOSABLE.** `ac_is_satisfied` returns on the doc-check branch before it ever looks at a covering AT, so **AT-11.5 could go green and this AC would not move**; and the only route the marker leaves is hand-writing a `yes` into this line's own inline satisfaction field, **which is a record written beside the artefact -- the exact form this criterion forbids.** Two routes on paper, zero in the gate, and the one the doc points at is the one the row prohibits. It was marked non-test by copying AC-11.1 to AC-11.4, which genuinely are doc checks; this row then acquired a real instrument and the marker did not follow. **`at lint` reports all rows conform over it.** L5 catches the mirror pairing -- a doc-check AT covering a test-backed AC -- and names the symptom exactly, _"an unclosable contract whose only symptom is a gate that will not move"_; **the reverse pairing produces the identical harm and is not checked.** Reported to hv rather than fixed here: `bin/**` is not vc's to edit. **AND THIS NOTE SATISFIED ITS OWN ROW ON THE FIRST WRITE (vc, caught in the same minute by the marker scan, gate 46 -> 47).** The sentence warning that a hand-written flag would close the row SPELLED the flag, and the parser cannot tell a row's data from a row's prose about its data -- **the document is its own format, so writing about a marker writes the marker.** This week's class again, at the smallest scale it has appeared: the measurement's subject and the report's subject were different, and the output could not tell them apart. **Nothing else in the contract does this today** -- the scan checks the whole table in both directions, and this was the only hit. **The gate cannot catch it: a row that hand-satisfies itself is a row that is satisfied**, and `at lint` reads all rows as conforming either way. **AND THIS ROW HAS NOW DONE IT TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, WITH TWO DIFFERENT TOKENS (vc).** The first note spelled the satisfaction field and CLOSED a row that must not close (gate 46 -> 47). **The note announcing that repair spelled the doc-check marker three times, and `ac_is_nontest` matches it ANYWHERE IN THE LINE (`bin/intent_acceptance:90`), so the repair undid itself and the row was unclosable again -- gate 46 while my own parser said 47.** **The disagreement is the only reason it surfaced, and it surfaced by luck: my scan reads the marker POSITIONALLY (immediately after the id) and the gate reads it anywhere, so for every row where the token appears only in its proper place the two agree exactly -- which is what they had been doing all session.** **Two readers of one format, agreeing until the first row that separates them.** The scan is being corrected to the gate's reading, because a checker that disagrees with the authority about what the data MEANS will keep certifying the authority's answer as its own. **The general form, and it is the day's class at the smallest possible scale: in a document that is its own data format, writing ABOUT a marker writes the marker -- so a note explaining a repair is itself a repair, in whichever direction the token points.**

**The shell implementation is pruned at the cut, and nothing in the repo EXECUTES or EMITS a `bin/` intent script path.** **RESCOPED 2026-08-15 (vc) on dc's measurement -- the original wording, _"nothing in the repo references `bin/` intent scripts"_, IS UNSATISFIABLE HONESTLY and a sweeper obeying it would destroy the record.** Measured: **337 tracked files reference `bin/intent*`, and 133 are records of the PAST** -- `intent/history/`, `intent/st/COMPLETED/`, whiteboard `.history/`, CHANGELOG, `done.md`. **A completed thread saying "we changed `bin/intent_helpers`" is a true statement about 2026, and rewriting it to make a criterion go green falsifies the record.** The remaining 167 are four different things and only one is a defect: **(1) provenance citations in comments** -- the overwhelming majority, `render.rs` / `views.rs` / `facade.rs` / `contract.rs` each naming the v2 line a behaviour was ported from; **a citation to a deleted file is still a true citation, and deleting them destroys the only means anyone has of re-deriving the parity decisions**. **(2) executable dependencies** -- the real prune target, and it is SMALL and CONCENTRATED: `intent/plugins/claude/bin/*` sourcing `bin/intent_helpers` plus `plugins/claude/lib`, **all of which is WP-07's, so this half may be discharged by WP-07 landing rather than by a WP-12 sweep**. **(3) parity fixtures** (`intent/st/ST0056/parity/**`, 42 files) -- reference data describing v2 behaviour, and **if they are the migration's evidence they must outlive the thing they describe**; a WP-12 call, not a sweep target. **(4) emitted strings** -- the genuine defect class, since a v2 path in a remedy names a file the user cannot possibly have. **(4) IS EMPTY, measured**: the sole candidate, `transitions.rs:264`'s `note:` carrying `bin/intent_acceptance:987`, sits on the `Unbuilt` enum variant with ZERO read sites -- the same shape as AC-00.9's own `Entry.v2` correction, and it looked like a second instance of that defect in the very file AC-00.9 named. **Nothing in the v3 binary emits a v2 script path.** **Classes (1) and the 133 historical records are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE of this criterion** and are named here so that nobody satisfying it deletes them. **Already discharged by construction**: `close_gate_parity.rs:505,575,655` probe for `bin/intent` and skip the live differential when it is absent (_"post-cutover tree?"_), so those three survive the prune without a WP-12 edit
Docs converged: working-with-llms.md, canon narrative, README, CHANGELOG
Release docs written BEFORE the cut so the tag carries them
v3.0.0 tagged on both remotes, GitHub release published, formula live

**(hv-RATIFIED 2026-08-15 as D31 -- was vc-specced under standing authorisation, which is what blocked ic's register row)** `treeindex` and the `in-handoff` skill are retired whole -- command, `intent/.treeindex/` cache, `/in-essentials` rules 3 and 4, and every canon reference -- and nothing in the repo references either
The index scope is the gitignore-aware repository, not `intent/**`: a source file is indexed, and a gitignored file never appears in any result
Lexical (FTS5) search returns hits across prose and source in the one result shape `{path, span, kind, tier, score, snippet}`
Structural (tree-sitter) search returns definition and reference hits for every language in the project's `languages` array, and a language absent from that array loads no grammar
The two-corpora staleness policy holds: `intent/**` hashes always (D24), the source corpus is stat-then-hash, and each is asserted against its own missed-edit case
A stale or partial index is named at query time or the query refuses with the remedy; a confident subset is never returned
intentd maintains the index incrementally in the background, and a daemonless query returns identical results to a daemon-served one
The MCP search tool and `intent search` return the same result shape from the same index -- one surface, two skins
T3 (semantic) and T4 (type-aware) are specified in design.md as staged additions, with S1-S5 shown sufficient to admit them without changing the CLI contract or the MCP tool schema

`wb_node`, `wb_item` and `wb_message` are model entities with schema faces, held in the DB per the reversed D01, and **sync round-trips them losslessly in both directions**: db-to-disk then disk-to-db reproduces the DB content, and the regenerated files are byte-identical to the committed ones. (Reworded 2026-08-15 for D01's reversal. The original asserted a `rm intent.db` rebuild from committed JSON canon; the property under test is now the round-trip rather than the rebuild, and it is a stronger claim because it binds both directions)
`wip.md` and `inbox.<sender>.md` are 100% generated views: regeneration reproduces the committed bytes exactly, through the repository formatter and not merely through the renderer
An over-bound write is refused by name, stating the bound and the remedy; nothing is truncated and nothing over-bound is accepted, with a body one byte over the limit as the discriminating case
Every timestamp is read from the clock by the API, and a caller-supplied timestamp is refused rather than honoured -- the fabricated-stamp class closed by construction, not by detection
The single-writer invariant is enforced by the API rather than by convention: a node writing another node's board, or an inbox it does not own, is refused
Archival is the API's: handled messages and completed DOING items transition on schedule, and no node action is required for a board to stay within its bounds
Every `/in-whiteboard` verb is served by `intent wb` from the store, in-process and over GraphQL, and any workstream can read any node's board
Boards and inboxes are FTS-indexed and reachable from `intent search` with the same result shape as the rest of the corpus
The existing three-node board migrates into the model with nothing dropped silently: what cannot be carried is named per item, and the count of carried items reconciles against the source
`/in-whiteboard` and the `intent claude ws` family are updated in this WP, so the protocol documents no workflow the tool refuses

No modelled entity carries a caller-authored timestamp (D33, project-wide and not whiteboard-local): every stamped field is written by the SERVICE layer from the clock at the moment of the event, **once**, and is never re-derived by a later sync in EITHER direction. A DB-side column default is refused as the mechanism: with the DB as truth (D01 as reversed) and sync running both ways, a disk-to-db resync that re-inserts rows lets `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` re-stamp them, rewriting history silently and indistinguishably from a correct value -- the fabricated-stamp failure shape reintroduced by its own fix. Discriminating case: stamp an entity, record the value, round-trip it through db-to-disk and disk-to-db, assert byte-identical -- a test that only asserts a stamp EXISTS after the round-trip passes on the defect. (Reworded 2026-08-15: the original argued this from the DB being rebuildable, which D01's reversal removed; the requirement survives with its reasoning inverted, which is why it is now stated independently of which side is durable)

**A WRITE PATH WHOSE INPUT WAS REFUSED MUST NOT THEN BE USED AS A SOURCE OF TRUTH.** (vc 2026-08-18, from a live instance with vc as the cause.) `sync --to-store` refused a canon extract on a `UNIQUE constraint failed: tests.thread_id, tests.id` and left the store at its previous contents. **`sync --to-disk` then wrote that stale store over canon at rc=0, with nothing in its output indicating the store had rejected the most recent write -- destroying the same authored criterion twice.** The two verbs are documented as opposite directions of one operation and nothing carries the failure of one into the other. **The property required is that the store record whether its last ingest SUCCEEDED, and that any egest from a store whose last ingest was REFUSED either refuse in turn or say so in its output.** A silent rc=0 egest from a known-stale store is a data-loss path that presents as a routine sync. **DISTINCT SUBJECT FROM AC-03.5/AC-03.6 (ic 2026-08-18, catching this before the wrong remedy was cited): those govern ATTACHMENT bytes against a commit; this episode destroyed a CRITERION, which no attachment check reaches.**

**A REBUILD INTO THE SHARED ARTEFACT PATH IS REFUSED WHEN THE TREE IS DIRTY WITH PATHS THE BUILDER DOES NOT OWN.** (cc + ic 2026-08-18, both declining to propose the row; vc mints it.) **`native/rust/target/release/` is shared by four nodes and there is NO per-node isolation underneath it**, so the only control that currently exists over what enters it is the convention _do not rebuild while I am measuring_. **A control that looks like a courtesy is the one that gets dropped the first time somebody is in a hurry** -- which is approximately what happened on 2026-08-18, with nobody being careless: a build at 19:33Z from a live tree carrying uncommitted WP-01 source produced a binary that resolved canon at a path the reverted source no longer used, and it emptied the store for every node until rebuilt. **TWO MITIGATIONS WERE OFFERED AND THE SECOND IS RULED: building from a clean extract PREVENTS the bad artefact; refusing a dirty cross-owner rebuild prevents it AND TELLS SOMEONE WHY, before the artefact exists, rather than producing a working-looking binary four nodes then invoke.** Failing loudly at the right moment beats failing silently at the cheap one.

**A WRITE MOVES MTIME ON EXACTLY THE FILES WHOSE BYTES CHANGED, AND NO OTHERS.** (cc 2026-08-18, third formulation; the row reached its fifth version because vc named the wrong ROW, cc the wrong SUBJECT, then the wrong PROPERTY, then vc the wrong DENOMINATOR.) Measured over the FILE ESTATE before and after -- snapshot `(path -> bytes, mtime)`, run the verb, snapshot again, assert `{p : mtime differs} == {p : bytes differ}` AS SETS. **The denominator is the ESTATE and never the `WriteSet`**: `WriteSet` is internal, so a test reading its denominator from the type would satisfy this row while `intent sync` stayed broken, and would additionally be blind to any write that never joins a set. **Measured at every USER-VISIBLE verb that writes the estate, with the verb set ENUMERATED AND PRINTED**, so a verb added later and not covered is visible rather than silently absent. **31 at minting** (cc, mapped rather than guessed): 27 through the nine `apply` sites -- `st new`; `st start|done|cancel|triage|hold|resume|reopen|reinstate`; `wp new`; `wp rescope`; `wp start|done|reopen|unstart`; `ac satisfy|unsatisfy|descope|rescope|withdraw|reinstate`; `at green|red|na`; `issues add`; `issues close|open` -- plus `sync --to-disk`, `sync --to-store`, `todo update`, `upgrade`, across six commit sites (`facade.rs:768`, `:1023`, `:1084`, `:1192`, `:2676`, `migrate.rs:338`). `ac gate` was flagged unverified by cc and is NOT among them: verified by vc at `render.rs:788` to read and print only. **WHY _RUN TWICE WRITES ZERO FILES_ IS NOT THE CRITERION** (cc, the correction that matters): it is INAPPLICABLE to the nine `apply` verbs, where the churn is worst and where zero-moved is legitimately FALSE, since the mutated thread's rows genuinely change. A row built on the no-op case leaves the worst-affected verbs outside the denominator WHILE LOOKING COVERED. Zero-on-a-no-op is a COROLLARY; it was only ever the easiest instance to measure, never the property. **THE LIVE VIOLATION AT MINTING**: `apply` calls `projection(&next, &changed_threads, &changed_issues)` -- canon JSON correctly narrow, but views render from FULL canon at `facade.rs:1272`, so **every mutating verb rewrites all 266 views to change about two**, and `intent st start` touches 266 files. `WriteSet::commit` then writes every path unconditionally through `write_atomically`'s temp-plus-rename, **which moves mtime BY CONSTRUCTION because it swaps in a new inode**. Measured: a no-op sync moved 20/20 views, twice, against a pre-registered prediction that the second run would be quiet. **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT** (cc, and this belongs in the rationale rather than the report): AC-03.2 -- view determinism, same model, same bytes, twice -- is satisfied by the churn PERFECTLY. The estate HAD an idempotence criterion and this defect is invisible to it by construction. **Not that nobody wrote a check: the check that exists is complete and correct about its own subject while the thing beside it rots.** `views::write_all` carries a correct unchanged-skip and has NO PRODUCTION CALLER -- all 18 call sites are under `tests/` -- and `view_determinism.rs` drives it directly and is green throughout. **THE STATED COST OF THE EARLIER FORM WAS FALSE** (cc 2026-08-18, against their own sentence, found by re-measuring it instead of citing it): `write_all`'s doc claimed the mtime move corrupts `file_index`'s clean/changed state. **It does not** -- `sync.rs:317-326` decides `FileState` from SHA-256 alone and the module doc says stat is never a gate, on vc's 2026-08-14 contract-governs ruling. The real costs are that the criterion is ratified and unmet, that it defeats every external mtime instrument, and that touching hundreds of files per verb is the opposite of what ST0057 is about. **THE FIX IS ONE SKIP AT THE ONE WRITER**: `WriteSet::commit` already reads the prior content via `record()` for rollback, so the comparison is free and `written: false` is already the exact semantics for nothing-to-undo. `projection` being shared by three of the six commit sites is what makes one skip cover them all. Red-first must be driven at the VERB over the file estate -- never through `organize` (retired in v3), never a per-thread projection (a subset that happens to be wholly changed goes green against an unguarded writer), never `write_all`, never one verb.

**A VERB THAT WOULD REDUCE A POPULATION TO ZERO MUST REFUSE OR NAME IT; SUCCEEDING AT rc=0 IS NOT AVAILABLE.** (ic 2026-08-18, from vc's live instance.) `sync --to-disk` wrote empty views over a non-empty estate at rc=0: `steel_threads.md` 57 rows -> 0, `todo.md` 82 -> 0. **NOTHING WAS REFUSED AND NOTHING MALFUNCTIONED IN THE EGEST** -- the store legitimately held zero threads, because a shared `target/release/` binary built from a reverted WP-01 tree had ingested zero and `sync --to-store` had reported success over it. The egest wrote exactly what it was given, correctly, by its own lights. **THIS IS NOT AC-03.13**, which requires an ingest to have been REFUSED; here nothing was refused, which is precisely why that row does not reach this and why the two are separate criteria rather than one. **The property is that a write which would empty a non-empty face must refuse or say so in its output.** **ic's own note is why this row is worth more than most tonight: it is the only finding of the evening whose positive control actually works** -- 57 and 82 are non-zero, observable before the verb runs, and cannot be confused with a correct answer, unlike a zero that is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty population. **Same class one verb upstream**: `sync --to-store` printing _the store and the extract agree_ over `0 == 0` is an instrument reporting success over an empty population, and this row is what that class looks like when the downstream verb is destructive.

**NO GENERATED VIEW NAMES A GENERATED ARTEFACT AS A SOURCE OF TRUTH.** (hv 2026-08-18, who sampled ONE cover and hit a generator defect; minted by vc on hv's ruling. Measured at `40d27ba2`.) **`views.rs:329` emits _Acceptance Criteria and Acceptance Tests live in `acceptance.md` -- the single source of truth_, and `:653` emits the WP-level twin.** Under the ratified model `acceptance.md` is a GENERATED VIEW of `thread.json`; the store is durable truth (D01 as reversed) and the committed extract is the interchange (D34). **`acceptance.md` is truth of nothing.** **THIS IS A WORK-LOSS INSTRUCTION, NOT A WORDING DEFECT, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS A CRITERION.** A reader who ACTS on it authors an AC row in `acceptance.md`; **that row is discarded at the next `--to-disk`.** The document instructs the exact action the model punishes, and nothing currently refuses it. **THE GENERATOR EMITS BOTH HALVES OF A CONTRADICTION IN ONE RUN**: the cover names `acceptance.md` as truth, while `acceptance.md`'s own footer -- same generator, same run -- reads _Generated by Intent v3.0.0-dev from `thread.json`. Do not edit this file._ **Neither file is wrong about itself; the pair cannot both be true in a reader's model.** **EXTENT, MEASURED AND STATED SO IT IS NOT INHERITED: 57 of 57 ST covers and 149 of 150 WP covers -- 206 of 207.** The single WP that escapes is not noise and not a round number: `carries_heading(&wp.body, "Acceptance")` suppresses the emit where a body supplies its own heading, **so the exception is the conditional working and it is what proves the population was counted rather than assumed.** **INSTRUMENT: THE CHECK READS EMITTED VIEWS AND RESOLVES WHAT EACH NAMED PATH IS -- NEVER THE GENERATOR'S STRING LITERALS.** The two would answer oppositely: rephrasing the literal while still naming a generated path passes a source grep and leaves the defect intact. **The generator knows every path it writes, so _a truth-claim naming one of its own outputs_ is mechanically decidable.** **AND A PHRASE GREP BOTH OVER- AND UNDER-REACHES, WHICH IS THE DENOMINATOR TRAP THIS ESTATE KEEPS PAYING FOR.** `views.rs` carries three occurrences of _truth_; **`:382` (_storing it would be double truth_) is CORRECT** -- satisfaction is computed from covering green ATs and never stored. **The denominator is every truth-claim the generator emits, not every hit of one phrase**, and a check keyed to the phrase would flag the correct one and miss any defect worded differently.
